Read-only fields hold values that must not change: the DeviceInfo structure markers, the device-specific security cache, and reserved and padding areas.
A wrong value can make the bootloader reset the whole DeviceInfo or stop the device from booting, and it may not be possible to undo.

view_bootloader_risks:
Changing the bootloader lock state wrongly can stop the device from booting. In particular, relocking while modified images such as TWRP or a rooted boot are installed can fail AVB verification and block boot.
When unlocked, verifiedbootstate changes to Orange, which may lower the security trust level of services such as Play Integrity and Widevine DRM.
User data must always be reset after an unlock or relock. A reset erases all user data on the device, so back it up first.

view_bootloader_what_the_task_does: Only the two flags change; every other DeviceInfo value stays as it is. If both flags are already in the chosen state, DeviceInfo is not written. The original configuration is restored automatically afterwards.
